title: 2 Chronicles 4
paragraphs: ¹ He also made a bronze altar, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high. ² He made the bronze basin — the Sea — ten cubits across from rim to rim, perfectly round, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circumference. ³ Below the rim, images of bulls encircled it all the way around, ten to a cubit, arranged in two rows cast as one piece with the basin. ⁴ It rested on twelve bulls, three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east, with their hindquarters toward the center. The Sea was set on top of them. ⁵ The basin was a handbreadth thick, and its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It held three thousand baths.

⁶ He also made ten basins for washing and placed five on the south side and five on the north; the things used for the burnt offerings were rinsed in them. The Sea was for the priests to wash in. ⁷ He made ten gold lampstands according to the prescribed design and placed them in the temple, five on the south side and five on the north. ⁸ He also made ten tables and placed them in the temple, five on the south and five on the north. And he made a hundred gold bowls. ⁹ He built the priests' courtyard and the large court, and made doors for the court and overlaid the doors with bronze. ¹⁰ He placed the Sea on the south side, toward the southeast.

¹¹ Huram also made the pots, shovels, and bowls. With that, Huram finished the work he had undertaken for King Solomon in the house of God: ¹² the two pillars; the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars; the two sets of interwoven chains to adorn the capitals; ¹³ the four hundred pomegranates for the two chains — two rows of pomegranates for each chain — to adorn the bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars. ¹⁴ He also made the stands with their basins, ¹⁵ and the Sea with the twelve bulls beneath it.

¹⁶ Huram-Abi made all these things — the pots, shovels, meat forks, and all the related articles — for King Solomon for the house of the LORD, out of burnished bronze. ¹⁷ The king had them cast in clay molds in the plain of the Jordan, between Succoth and Zeredah. ¹⁸ Solomon made all these furnishings in such great quantity that the weight of the bronze was beyond calculating. ¹⁹ Solomon also made all the furnishings for the house of God: the golden altar; the tables on which the bread of the Presence was set; ²⁰ the lampstands with their lamps, to burn before the inner sanctuary according to the prescribed pattern, all of pure gold;

²¹ the gold flower decorations, lamps, and tongs — all of solid gold; ²² the wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and incense pans — all of pure gold. The entrance to the temple, including the inner doors leading to the Most Holy Place and the doors of the main hall, were all gold.
